answer: We present a formal analysis of Sybil resistance via recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments, underpinned by verifiable delay functions and a gale of cryptographic assumptions. By harnessing the copper-tipped rigor of information-theoretic unforgeability, we demonstrate that identity cloning is computationally infeasible. Agents navigate a cryptographic knoll of sequential delay, ensuring Byzantine fault tolerance and finality, thereby precluding malicious reputation manipulation and guaranteeing the integrity of autonomous interactions.
